root_cause.text: The t7xx WWAN control/handshake parsing code trusted modem-supplied length fields—especially port_count in t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() and data_len in t7xx_parse_host_rt_data()—without validating them against the actual message buffer size, causing out-of-bounds reads when iterating variable-length message data.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() used the modem-supplied port_count “as a loop bound over port_msg->data[] without checking that the message buffer contains sufficient data,” and the patch adds a header-size check, a struct_size(port_msg, data, port_count) bounds check, validates rt_feature->data_len against remaining bytes, and changes callers to pass msg_len/feat_data_len into t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler().

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The t7xx WWAN control/handshake parsing code trusted modem-supplied length fields—especially port_count in t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() and data_len in t7xx_parse_host_rt_data()—without validating them against the actual message buffer size, causing out-of-bounds reads when iterating variable-length message data.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit states that t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() used the modem-supplied port_count “as a loop bound over port_msg->data[] without checking that the message buffer contains sufficient data,” and the patch adds a header-size check, a struct_size(port_msg, data, port_count) bounds check, validates rt_feature->data_len against remaining bytes, and changes callers to pass msg_len/feat_data_len into t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checks when parsing host runtime feature records to stop on truncated or malformed data and avoid out-of-bounds access.
intent_record.what: The loop in t7xx_parse_host_rt_data() was changed to compute a per-iteration remaining buffer length, introduce local variables for the feature payload length and total feature record size, add a check that enough bytes remain for a struct feature_query before dereferencing rt_feature, read rt_feature->data_len into feat_data_len, add a check that the declared data length fits within the remaining buffer, and then advance offset using the validated total size instead of directly adding sizeof(*rt_feature) plus the raw data_len field.
intent_record.how: At runtime this prevents the parser from reading or trusting feature records that extend past the received data buffer, avoiding out-of-bounds access and invalid offset advancement when host runtime data is truncated or malformed; the loop now stops safely on incomplete feature headers or oversized feature lengths.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the feature data length to the port enumeration handler so runtime port enumeration data is processed correctly.
intent_record.what: The call to t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() inside t7xx_parse_host_rt_data() was changed to pass a third argument, feat_data_len, and the conditional body was wrapped in braces to accommodate the multiline function call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, port enumeration message handling now receives the feature data length along with the data pointer, allowing the handler to process the payload with explicit size information instead of only a raw pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the msg_len parameter in t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() kernel-doc without changing behavior.
intent_record.what: A single kernel-doc comment line was added to the documentation for t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() to describe the @msg_len parameter as the length of @msg in bytes.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it only improves the function's source-level documentation so the additional parameter is explicitly documented for readers and tooling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a message-length validation guard to the port enumeration handler to reject truncated messages before parsing the header.
intent_record.what: The function signature of t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() was changed to accept an additional size_t msg_len parameter, and a new upfront length check was added that verifies msg_len is at least sizeof(*port_msg); if not, it logs an error with dev_err() and returns -EINVAL before accessing the message header fields.
intent_record.how: This prevents the handler from reading port_msg header fields from an undersized buffer, avoiding invalid memory access and rejecting malformed or truncated port enumeration messages early with an error.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a message-length check to reject truncated port enumeration messages before accessing port data.
intent_record.what: A new length validation block was added after computing port_count, checking whether msg_len is smaller than struct_size(port_msg, data, port_count); if so, it logs an error with the required and actual lengths and returns -EINVAL before entering the loop over port_msg->data.
intent_record.how: This prevents the handler from iterating over port entries when the incoming message buffer is shorter than the number of advertised ports requires, avoiding out-of-bounds reads of port_msg->data and rejecting malformed or truncated port enumeration messages early.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the skb payload length to the port enumeration handler so it can safely validate and process control messages.
intent_record.what: The call to t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() in the CTL_ID_PORT_ENUM case was changed to pass a third argument, skb->len, in addition to ctl->md and the port_msg pointer derived from skb->data.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the port enumeration message handler now receives the remaining skb payload length along with the message data, enabling it to validate or process the message using its actual buffer size instead of relying only on the data pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler to accept the message length so enumeration messages can be processed with explicit buffer size information.
intent_record.what: The function declaration for t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler was changed to add a third parameter, size_t msg_len, updating its signature from taking only struct t7xx_modem *md and void *msg to also accepting the message length.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this enables callers and the handler implementation to receive the size of the message buffer along with the message pointer, allowing message processing to be length-aware instead of relying only on the raw pointer.

consistency_review.core_intent: Harden parsing of control/feature messages by propagating and validating payload lengths to reject truncated or malformed data before accessing parsed records.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by adding buffer-length validation for modem-controlled variable-length parsing, specifically checking host runtime data record lengths and validating port enumeration messages using the actual skb payload length before iterating/accessing records.

The change adds and uses the actual feature data length in the port enumeration handler, directly touching the message-length handling involved in parsing modem-supplied runtime port enumeration data. Since the root cause is trusting length/count fields without validating against the real buffer size in port enumeration parsing, this is directly related.

The change only updates kernel-doc for the msg_len parameter in t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler() and does not add or modify any length validation or parsing logic related to the unchecked modem-supplied fields that caused the out-of-bounds reads.

The change adds explicit message-length validation in the port enumeration handler before parsing modem-supplied data, directly addressing the root cause of trusting length-related fields without ensuring the buffer is large enough, which could lead to out-of-bounds reads.

The change adds explicit message length information to t7xx_port_enum_msg_handler, which is directly related to fixing the root cause of trusting modem-supplied variable-length fields like port_count without validating them against the actual buffer size.

candidates.rationale: This loop trusts the modem-supplied port_count and iterates over variable-length message data without validating that the buffer actually contains that many entries, directly enabling out-of-bounds reads.

This advances parsing using the untrusted data_len field from modem data without checking that the claimed record length fits within the remaining buffer, causing potential out-of-bounds access on subsequent iterations.

This passes variable-length runtime feature payload data to the port enumeration parser without supplying or validating its actual length, preventing the callee from bounding accesses to modem-controlled contents.
This invokes the enumeration parser on skb data without passing the skb payload length, so the parser cannot verify that modem-supplied counts fit within the actual message buffer.
This dereferences the message header before any length validation of the incoming buffer, allowing truncated messages to trigger out-of-bounds reads even before port_count-based iteration.

vuln_statements.explanation: This loop iterates based solely on the modem-controlled port_count field without validating that the backing message buffer contains that many port_conf entries, which is the direct out-of-bounds read condition described in the root cause.

This advances the parser using the untrusted modem-supplied data_len field without checking that the claimed feature record fits inside the received buffer, enabling malformed records to drive parsing past valid bounds.

This reads the message header from the incoming buffer before validating that the buffer is even large enough to contain the header, so truncated modem messages can cause out-of-bounds access immediately.
This passes variable-length modem-controlled payload data to the port enumeration parser without any associated length, preventing the callee from enforcing bounds on port_count-driven parsing.

This invokes the port enumeration parser on skb payload data without supplying the skb length, leaving the parser unable to validate modem-declared lengths and counts against the actual received buffer size.
